text: At the end of every seven years you shall grant a release of debts.

This is how the release shall work: every creditor shall release what he has lent to his neighbor. He shall not press his neighbor or his brother for payment, because the LORD's release has been proclaimed.
You may press a foreigner for payment, but whatever your brother owes you, you shall release.
However, there will be no poor among you, for the LORD will surely bless you in the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess—

versions.text: There will be no poor among you, however, for the LORD will surely bless you in the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess—
versions.explanation: The Hebrew אֶפֶס stands at the head of the sentence as a contrastive marker. Placing "however" mid-sentence after a comma breaks the rhythm for oral reading; moving it to the front reads more naturally and matches the Hebrew word order.

text: if only you listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God, taking care to follow all this commandment that I am giving you today.
For the LORD your God will bless you as he has promised, and you will lend to many nations but borrow from none; you will rule over many nations, but none will rule over you.
If there is a poor man among you, one of your brothers, in any of your towns in the land the LORD your God is giving you, do not harden your heart or shut your hand against your brother in his need.
Rather, open your hand wide to him and lend him freely whatever he needs.

Be careful that no wicked thought creeps into your heart, such as: "The seventh year, the year of release, is near"—so that you look grudgingly at your brother in need and give him nothing. Then he will cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
Give to him generously and without a grudging heart, for because of this the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in everything you set your hand to.
For there will always be poor people in the land. That is why I command you: open your hand wide to your brother, to the needy and the poor in your land.

versions.text: There will never cease to be poor in the land. That is why I command you: open your hand wide to your brother, to the needy and the poor in your land.
versions.explanation: "There will never cease to be poor in the land" is stilted for reading aloud, and "poor" without a noun is ambiguous. A positive rendering conveys the same sense of the Hebrew ("the needy will not cease from the midst of the land") with better flow.

text: If one of your own people, a Hebrew man or woman, is sold to you and serves you six years, in the seventh year you shall let that person go free from you.

versions.text: If one of your own people, a Hebrew man or woman, is sold to you and serves you six years, in the seventh year you shall set him free.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew includes מֵעִמָּךְ ("from you"), which is left untranslated here though it is rendered in verse 13. Also, since the verse expressly mentions a man or a woman, "him" is inconsistent; a neutral rendering keeps the sentence coherent.

text: And when you set him free, do not send him away empty-handed.
Supply him generously from your flock, your threshing floor, and your winepress. Give to him as the LORD your God has blessed you.
Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt and the LORD your God redeemed you. That is why I am giving you this command today.
But if he says to you, "I will not leave you," because he loves you and your household and is content with you,
then take an awl and drive it through his ear into the door, and he will be your servant for life. Do the same for your female servant.

versions.text: then take an awl and pierce his ear against the door, and he will be your servant for life. Do the same for your female servant.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew says the awl is put "into his ear and into the door," that is, driven through the ear into the doorpost. "Pierce his ear against the door" obscures that the awl passes into the door itself.

text: Do not think it a hardship to set him free, for his six years of service have been worth twice the wages of a hired hand. And the LORD your God will bless you in all you do.
Set apart to the LORD your God every firstborn male of your herds and flocks. Do not put the firstborn of your oxen to work, and do not shear the firstborn of your flock.
Year after year you and your household shall eat it in the presence of the LORD your God at the place the LORD will choose.
But if it has any defect—if it is lame or blind, or has any serious flaw—you shall not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
You may eat it in your own town. Both the unclean and the clean may eat it, as they would a gazelle or a deer.
Only you must not eat its blood; pour it out on the ground like water.
